newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end quietly mixed eyeing EMU moves.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end quietly mixed eyeing EMU moves.

text.p: Italian stocks ended little changed in a thin market on Thursday after a session of range trading with the market awaiting details of the government's three year economic target plan on Friday and the outcome of the French elections runoff on Sunday.
"We're watching the result of the French vote, and now also in light of the Bundesbank/Bonn row, to try to fathom out the likely developments on the EMU front," one trader said.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 0.03 percent off at 12,238 but the Mib30 blue chip index managed a modest 0.07 percent gain to 18,213.
"There are a lot of different opinions over the effects on the Bourse of problems linked to the single European currency," this trader added.

Fiat gained 0.27 percent to 5,616 lire but some analysts said they had expected more after chairman Cesare Romiti spoke earlier this week of 1997 turnover up to some 90 trillion lire and after Merrill Lynch raised its rating to accumulate.
Eni held up, gaining 0.25 percent to 8,718 lire, even if operators generally expected the price to ease ahead of the energy group's third tranche share placement next month.
Telecoms were mixed with only mobile operator TIM up.
In insurances, Ras continued weaker to touch a new low for the year at 13,100 lire, closing down 1.19 percent at 13,136.
Jeweller Bulgari saw continued buying interest in view of an upcoming share split and closed 3.15 percent up at 33,766 lire having touched a new year's high at 34,000.
In clothing and textiles stocks, Benetton gained 1.25 percent to 23,529 lire and Marzotto put on 0.37 percent to 14,007 but Stefanel lost 0.62 percent to 2,579.
In banks, Mediobanca, Banca Commerciale Italiana, Banco Ambrosiano Veneto and San Paolo all slipped but Credito Italiano gained 0.87 percent to 2,547.
